THE PREAMBLE, verbatim:
## Slice two units

One row is one PR, from main, signed and through the merge queue after the
operator rules. Follow this order. Dependencies are semantic prerequisites,
not simply the preceding row; the independence of U1–U4 is explicit in D9.
No row through U9a lifts the MCP compile fence. U9b is the sole enabling PR.
The lettered splits are required by the checked seams: record schema plus

protocol and adapter data; storage/folding/inspect crosses CLI, protocol,
runtime and pure view. Minimal ledger writing is deliberately pulled into U6.

`contracts/realms.v<N>.schema.json` denotes one exact future file allocated
as **the next realms version after v7** at U5c, including v7's fields. It is
the only intentionally deferred filename number. Every other production path
below is literal. New paths are proposed modules/schemas, not files created
by this document plan. Constructors/registration are counted in their row.
Future tests extend the named suites; capability_broker already exists under
the consolidated CLI integration binary. New capability_artifacts and runtime
capability_ledger/capability_broker_launch modules are registered through the
existing test-only roots (CLI tests/it.rs and runtime tests/it.rs), not new
undeclared binaries. Tests may use child modules of the owning suites to stay

Each row closes exactly its numbered tasks, including tests/mutations and
gate evidence. Test lists below are the allowed owning suites; every row
also updates this change's tasks and later implementation evidence. Measured

YOUR UNIT, verbatim:
### U7c — Provision protected per-attempt plans

Provision the single sealed plan inventory and private roots before launch, with complete owner identity and disjoint fixed retention shares including permitted fallback slots. Reuse existing launch facts; do not add a duplicate capability inventory or launch state machine. In marks.rs project and clear selected server/tool/discovery identifiers from the same intent consumed by configuration, using existing adapter hands.notice facts. Carry no plan or storage locator into prompt rendering; parse new edge data once into types.

Prepare box facts through U6c4/U6c5's existing consumed API: effective selected hands/Git roots, source identities/digest, mapped writer/privilege facts, closed system-entry/package-entry tree, trusted bootstrap and store/control exclusions. Project the existing typed egress once into network disposition and bind the already judged clearance receipt to the policy digest. Seal these facts for each selected fallback/member/step without serializing live handles; the broker reobserves before lookup. Runtime observes the host above pure core/view and never uses a display admission function. Drift is a hard failure, including for wants; tests mutate each bound fact independently.

Closes tasks 35.1 and 35.2; requirements [SD3](specs/slice-two-delivery/spec.md), [MB1](specs/mcp-capability-broker/spec.md), [MB3](specs/mcp-capability-broker/spec.md), [CR3](specs/capability-response-retention/spec.md).
Proof: Substitution/missing inventory/pre-start uncertainty refuse exactly; simultaneous slots cannot share quota, oversized allocation refuses before launch, and resume cannot create fresh budget. Bind selected-fact construction and clearing independently: fallback and wanted drop remove stale facts, original requested digest and native/no-MCP behavior stay unchanged, and prompt facts contain no secret-store/ledger locator.

Operator rulings 2026-10-15, after the blocked first run: U7c reads the network disposition, the clearance receipt and effective retention that U7c0 seals on each holding, and writes plans and the inventory through the protocol records' one `Serialize`. Retention shares are a fixed function of the sealed inventory: each retaining plan's share is 256 MiB divided by the number of retaining pins it lists, permitted fallback slots included, and provisioning refuses "capability evidence budget is exhausted" before launch where a share would fall under 8 MiB (more than 32 retaining slots). No inventory field carries them; U8b derives the same share from the same sealed inventory. The budget belongs to one attempt: its directory is created exclusively, so a retry, a reconnect or a resumed engine cannot mint a second inventory or fresh shares for an attempt, and re-provisioning an attempt whose directory exists refuses before launch; a resume that starts a new attempt has that attempt's own budget, as every attempt does. "Resume cannot create fresh budget" is proved as that refusal.

Operator rulings 2026-10-15, after the second run's review: U7c provisions each plan's box through U7c0b's verb, not `ServerBox::prepare`. Provisioning moves after the attempt's deadline is constructed; the engine writes the request, runs the current Brokkr binary's hidden verb as a child in its own process group under the startup deadline and the attempt's remaining bound, and on expiry or cancellation kills and reaps the group and refuses before launch with no driver started. The engine's remaining pre-spawn steps (the attempt directory, Git discovery for reach, the store path) are ordinary engine filesystem steps, as every attempt's hands setup is. U7c may add `McpContribution` to `crates/brokkr-runtime/src/bundle.rs`'s existing crate-visible `mcp` re-export, so marks.rs consumes the one projection instead of restating it; the public API does not change.

Operator rulings 2026-10-16, after the third run's review: the survey ends with the engine, whatever ends it. `crates/brokkr-cli/src/broker/survey.rs` (U7c0b's verb) may change so the survey ties its life to the engine as `serve`'s observer ties its own to the broker (`tethered`): it reads exactly one request line, then watches its standard input, which the engine holds open until it has the reply, and the end of that input kills the survey's whole process group. A stop signal that ends the engine before its stop handler exists, the handler's own stop, and the engine's death all end the survey with nothing left running; provisioning has no other cancellation source. The proof stops a real engine process mid-survey, by SIGTERM and by SIGKILL, and observes no survivor. U7c may also add rustix's `process` feature to `crates/brokkr-runtime/Cargo.toml`, the version brokkr-protocol and brokkr-cli already build with it, so `Cargo.lock` does not move, to kill and reap the survey's group on expiry without unsafe code.

Owning tests: `crates/brokkr-runtime/src/engine/capability_tests.rs`, `crates/brokkr-runtime/src/engine/resume_tests.rs`, `crates/brokkr-runtime/tests/capability_launch.rs`.

CONTROLLER'S STATE FOR THIS RUN (the-forge-67, 2026-10-16). This is U7c's FIFTH RUN.
- Run 4 (0065-slice-two-unit-u7c-see-the--ae14d2ff) built cdbc82f5; review returned REVIEW-RESIDUAL-OK (L1–L3, low) and it opened PR #713.
- CI and the controller's host check then found what the run's own gates could not: two test-only defects, which the controller fixed in a signed commit, 559c16e5, and two production defects, which are this run's job.
- Every suite passed on the host: runtime --lib 1010, --test capability_launch 76, --test it 132; cli --lib 856, --test it 688. With the controller's fix, exact coverage over the whole workspace reached 59122/59122 lines and 7868/7868 branches, but 7393/7395 FUNCTIONS, and the CRAP ratchet refused.

YOUR WORKTREE ARRIVES WITH BOTH COMMITS' WORK STAGED. prep replayed 6da7fc35..559c16e5 onto main, which has moved (8819b7ee or later), leaving out quality/file-lines.txt: regenerate it. KEEP the replay, including the controller's test fix exactly as it is: `profile` and `dep_info` in provision_tests/survey_tests.rs, which find the built brokkr and its dep-info under cargo's build-dir layout (the exact coverage gate's toolchain), and the Linux-only creation of the non-UTF-8 HOME directory in provision_tests.rs (macOS's APFS refuses that name with EILSEQ). Check the replay against main, fix the two defects below, rerun the gates, commit signed.

D1. FUNCTION COVERAGE. The exact gate counts functions, and two never run: the two closures in `Engine::provision` (crates/brokkr-runtime/src/engine/broker.rs, about lines 256–257): `live` (`|| Host::of(std::env::vars_os(), std::env::current_exe())`) and `survey` (`|bootstrap, request| surveyed(bootstrap, request, deadline)`). No test reaches them. Tests drive `provision_with` with stand-ins, and inside a test binary `current_exe()` is the test binary, so the real path can never run there. Remove both closures rather than adding a test that re-executes the test binary as a survey, which would recurse into libtest. The recommended shape, though any equivalent with no unreachable function is fine:
  - read the host eagerly in `provision` as a plain value (`Host::of(std::env::vars_os(), std::env::current_exe())`, cheap), and pass `Result<Host, Unprovisioned>` into `provision_with`/`provisioned`, which still consult it only after the budget and seals are judged and only where a site brokers a holding. A bad HOME must still refuse only such an attempt, never one with no brokered holding. Bind that with a test.
  - make the surveyor take the deadline (`Surveyor` = `&dyn Fn(&Path, &Survey, Instant) -> Result<Provisioned, Unprovisioned>`), and have `provision` pass `&surveyed` itself, which the survey tests already cover. Each stand-in in the tests takes the extra argument.
  - every line of `provision` then runs on every attempt the engine tests execute. Keep the existing tests' assertions.

D2. CYCLOMATIC COMPLEXITY. quality/crap-baseline.json holds `Engine::execute` (crates/brokkr-runtime/src/engine.rs) at cyclomatic 22.0. Your call `if !self.provision(ids, &selection, &mut deadline)? { return Ok(()); }` raised it to 24.0, and the ratchet refuses ("CC 24.0 over its baseline 22.0 (regressed)"). Never raise a baseline (operator standing rule). Bring execute back to 22 or below by moving an existing block, with its decision points, into a private helper in engine.rs or engine/broker.rs. Each `if`, `?`, `&&`, `||`, loop and extra match arm counts, so move out at least two. Good candidates are the provenance and boundary-entry recording just before `EffectStarted`, the ship-phase gate-head block, or the provisioning step folded together with the deadline and the results directory. Do NOT restructure execute's `match body` arms or the body-name match near its top: another session's PR (#709, story #349 slice 6) rewrites those `ExecutableBody` arms and lands after U7c. The helper you add must stay at or below the ratchet's limit and be fully covered. The controller measures CRAP on the host. You cannot run it (it needs the exact gate's LCOV), so count by hand and say your count in evidence.

ALSO, from run 4's review (low; fix if cheap, otherwise record):
- L2: record a compiling classification mutation binding survey/tests.rs `a_request_line_ending_inside_its_record_is_malformed` (its Malformed assertion failing, then restored and passing) in evidence/U7c.md.
- L3: evidence/U7c.md around lines 218–224 records only the removed Cancelled-text mutation for `each_provisioning_refusal_says_its_own_words`. Mutate a surviving refusal's text and record the current test failing, then passing.
- L1 (survey.rs maps failure to lead its group, and watcher-thread spawn failure, to Refusal::Identity): needs a protocol cause, which is outside this unit. Leave it, and keep it recorded under follow-ups.

Update evidence/U7c.md: state D1 and D2 and how each was closed, name the controller's commit 559c16e5 and what it fixed, and record a compiling removal for each new or changed test. Tick tasks 35.1/35.2 only on observed evidence.

STANDING RULINGS. Decision 0065's hold: off by default, no grandfathering; realm-only grants; tools are an abstraction, dialects the concrete; refuse, never reconcile (slice one's operator ruling of 2026-09-23). The MCP compile fence stays in place until U9b. Hosts are Linux and macOS only (decision 0063). Main's code-health rules bind: no `unsafe` in brokkr-runtime; `#[expect(.., reason)]`, never `#[allow]`; clippy's too_many_lines, excessive_nesting and struct_excessive_bools are denied, so split, and only if splitting would widen your unit carry `reason = "baseline 2026-09-29, decision 0065 slice one merged with main; split after #319"`; when a count moves, re-measure quality/'s file-lines, too-many-lines and suppressions (the steps quality/measure.sh uses), witness pins with `BROKKR_BLESS=1 cargo test -p brokkr-runtime --test witness_digests` (or, once #423's single test binary is on your base — crates/brokkr-runtime/tests/it.rs exists — `BROKKR_BLESS=1 cargo test -p brokkr-runtime --test it witness_digests::`), and budgets with scripts/measure-budgets.sh. Where a crate has tests/it.rs, a NEW tests/*.rs file must be registered as `mod <file>;` in that crate's tests/it.rs (layering::test_targets refuses an unregistered one), unless it sets HOME, cwd, env or a global allocator, in which case it is its own [[test]] in Cargo.toml with the reason written there; and `--test <file>` filters become `--test it <file>::` (capability_launch stays its own binary).

RULES. Touch at most the production files your row names; if the real scope exceeds them, STOP and report `oversized` with the split. One exception, the operator's standing rule of 2026-10-09 (operator-ruling-2026-10-03.md): beside a production file in your row that sits at its 800-line ceiling, or is frozen at its quality/file-lines.txt baseline above it, you may add NEW private child modules, declared from that file, in its own module tree and consumed in this unit, without stopping. The same holds beside a row file that your own change would push past 800 lines (extended 2026-10-11). You may also change an EXISTING private child module of a file in your row, in that file's own module tree (extended 2026-10-11). You may move existing code out of the full file into such a child to make room, preferring the code your change touches. Name each new file in your evidence and commit, and set its quality/file-lines.txt row. You may also add a name to an EXISTING re-export in the parent module that declares one of your row's files, where the parent's line count does not change (extended 2026-10-10). Files in any other module tree still mean `oversized`; any public API growth still needs the operator's ruling at PR time (record it, do not stop). Test files are NOT bounded by the row (controller's standing clarification, 2026-10-05): a test anywhere that pins behaviour your unit changes, a validator or fixture swap in another suite, or a new child test module beside an owning suite that sits over its line ceiling is part of your unit — size-neutral wherever a file sits at its quality/file-lines.txt baseline. A LOW finding you cannot fix inside your row's production files: record it in your result and do NOT report blocked for it. Tests assert exact reasons and values, never is_err(); every new test is bound by a compiling mutation that makes it fail, then restored, recorded (test, assertion) in evidence.md. Tick a task in tasks.md only on observed evidence; record results in a NEW file of your own, openspec/changes/decision-0065-capabilities-slice-two/evidence/U7c.md (two lanes deliver units at once, and every unit appending to evidence.md made each pair of pull requests conflict), and do not edit evidence.md itself; write it in prose or a table — never as a bullet list of the standard gate lines (`cargo fmt ...: clean`, `cargo clippy ...: clean`), which earlier evidence files already hold word for word, so the data clone gate refuses it; never edit the tasks.md preamble. Frozen contracts, policy/phase-machine.json, fixtures/, reference/ and extensions/ do not move unless your unit names them. Sign every commit (`git commit -S`; main requires signatures). HEADLESS SEAT: your session ends the moment you end a turn — never run a command in the background, never use Monitor or ScheduleWakeup, run every command in the foreground under the tool's 10-minute limit (suites crate by crate with `timeout 590`, split by --lib/--test if longer), and write your result file before you finish. GATES: cargo fmt --all -- --check; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings; the suite of each crate you touched; openspec validate --all --strict; typos --hidden; git diff --check; quality/ratchet.sh files and clones. instructions.analyze:
# OpenSpec analyze

Judge duplication, ambiguity, underspecification, house alignment, coverage gaps, and inconsistency across proposal, deltas, design and tasks. Treat the realm house as the constitution. Return each finding with severity and its earliest owning artifact; zero findings is consistent.
instructions.clarify:
# OpenSpec clarify

Judge underspecified areas, unquantified language, missing decisions, capability/delta mismatches, and requirements without adequate scenarios. Return every ambiguity with the evidence needed to settle it; zero findings is clear.
instructions.design:
# OpenSpec design

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/design.md`. Record context, goals and non-goals, decisions with alternatives, risks, migration, and open questions. On return, revise the design and dependent artifacts so no finding is merely acknowledged.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.

Change location: `openspec/changes/{change}`. Archive operation: ["openspec","archive","{change}","--yes"].

# OpenSpec archive

Folding a change is the last task: run the archive operation named above,
which moves the change directory under `openspec/changes/archive/` and
folds its deltas into `openspec/specs/`. Folding also records which change
wrote which capability, so every capability the change touched carries a
`## Provenance` list.

After the archive operation, open each capability's
`openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md` that the change touched and append
exactly one line under a `## Provenance` heading held at the end of the
file:

`- \`<archived-directory-name>\` — folded <YYYY-MM-DD>`

`<archived-directory-name>` is the directory the archive operation
created under `openspec/changes/archive/`; `<YYYY-MM-DD>` is the day it
was folded. Append only: never rewrite, reorder or remove an existing
provenance line, because standing truth accumulates and is not edited into
a different meaning. The line is a pointer, not a summary — it names the
change and nothing else, and the why stays in the change directory.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, and `reference/` (its schemas included) are
read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `recipes/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

The supported hosts are Linux and macOS (decision 0063); WSL2 is Linux. Write
no Windows-conditional code, test or evidence.

## Architecture

Decision 0071 rules how code here is shaped. Build to it, and cite its ruling
numbers in what you judge. Where a gate named below holds a rule, the gate is
the authority, and a finding it would catch is the gate's.

- **Pure core (ruling 1).** `brokkr-core` and `brokkr-view` do no I/O and read
  no clock, environment or randomness. They run no process. Pass `now`, paths
  and environment in as arguments. Effects live in the crates above core and
  view, and are journaled.
- **Enums and data, not traits (ruling 2).** A closed set is an enum matched
  exhaustively, with no wildcard arm that decides behaviour. Anything an
  operator extends is data under `adapters/`, `agents/`, `recipes/` or
  `realms.json`, validated and digested. Add a trait only for a seam whose
  contract spans several operations that must stay consistent with one
  another, reached across a process or service boundary, and name that seam
  in its doc comment. `ProducerTransport` is the one such trait today. A test
  double alone does not make a seam: a single substitutable function is a
  closure seam (`*_with`, `*_in`), which is how the house inverts a
  dependency otherwise.
- **Typed at the edge (ruling 3).** Parse wire, file and harness data once
  into a type, with `serde` and `deny_unknown_fields` where the contract is
  closed. `serde_json::Value` never goes past the edge, into state, or back
  out by string key. Never put `format!("{:?}")` in anything digested or
  journaled. A doubly-optional field or a string vocabulary is a missing enum.
- **Small functions (ruling 4).** New and changed functions stay within 100
  lines, nesting depth 5 and 7 parameters. Cyclomatic complexity follows
  the operator's 2026-09-26 ruling: a function may reach the higher of 15
  and its baseline, so a new function stays within 15, an existing one may
  change freely up to 15, and one already over 15 may only shrink.
  Production files stay within 800 lines and test files within 2,000, and a
  file already over may not grow. Add no new `jscpd` clone in production
  code, test code or data. `quality/` holds the measured baseline. Today's
  offenders carry `#[allow(clippy::…)]`, and #337 converts them to
  `#[expect(clippy::…, reason = "…")]`. Add a suppression only by a ruling,
  and remove it when you fix the function. A new suppression is
  `#[expect(…, reason)]`, never `#[allow]`.
- **Once (ruling 5).** Every fact has one home. A repeated vocabulary, skeleton
  or helper becomes one function or one table. An agent is defined once under
  `agents/`, and seats hire it by reference. A recipe that differs from another
  by a model, a seat or an entry is an `extends` overlay, never a copy. The
  agent library does not yet accept `extends`, and #360 builds it. Until then,
  a variation of an agent lives at the seat that hires it, overridden in a
  recipe overlay. It is never a second agent file that restates the first. A
  copy that must exist, such as a script a bundle pins, is held to its source
  by a test.
- **Nothing unused (ruling 6).** Add no alias, agent, contract version, flag or
  `pub` item without a consumer, and prefer `pub(crate)`. A deprecation names
  the release that removes it.
- **One derivation (ruling 7).** A fact shown on two surfaces is derived once
  in `brokkr-view`. The CLI, the TUI and `ui.html` only paint it. The engine
  never admits anything by a display-crate function.
- **Typed errors (ruling 8).** Return a `thiserror` enum whose `Display` keeps
  the operator's text. Tests match variants and pin each module's text once.
  Add no new `Result<_, String>`.
- **Tests that bind (ruling 9).** Assert exact values or variants, never
  `is_err()` alone. Show that every new test binds: a compiling mutation that
  removes the behaviour must make it fail. Restore the behaviour and record
  the failing test. Share fixtures through builders. Never change the process
  environment without a guard that restores it on unwind. A production guard
  left out because the exact-coverage gate would count it unreachable carries
  a removal-control test for the invariant that makes it unreachable, and the
  comment explaining the omission names that test.
- **The house's patterns (ruling 10).**
  - A harness is a module behind `AdapterKind`. This is the target form;
    today all five kinds share one module, and #347 and #348 build the
    split.
  - A CLI verb is a `Cmd` variant plus a handler.
  - A long parameter list becomes a parameter object.
  - Argv and mount tables are built with a builder.
  - Observing the world is split from deciding on it.
  - Never use a trait-object registry for a closed set.

Judges rate a finding against these rulings by this table, and cite the ruling
number:

- **info:** something a house gate would catch. The gate's verdict is the
  authority.
- **low:** a new or changed function over a ceiling, a rule written a second
  time, an item added without a consumer, or a `Value` carried past its edge
  within one module.
- **medium:** an untyped vocabulary that crosses crates, recipe or agent data
  copied instead of extended, a fact derived a second time on another surface,
  an error matched by its text, or a new test that cannot fail.
- **high or above:** any violation that hides a fail-open path or weakens a
  refusal. It is carried as a security finding.

A principle the implementer bent knowingly, and named with its reason in
`notes`, is still rated, and the judge carries that reason with the finding.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.

  "version_files": ["Cargo.toml", "Cargo.lock"],

members.adversarial:
Security review of the U7c fifth run (commit 968e6a51, signed G, vs base 8819b7ee). Scope: the whole single U7c commit (engine.rs, engine/broker.rs, engine/marks.rs, bundle.rs re-export, brokkr-runtime Cargo.toml, cli broker/survey.rs) plus the isolated D1/D2 diff (559c16e5..HEAD) and the new/changed tests. No production file outside the unit's row moved; Cargo.lock is byte-unchanged; no unsafe, no unwrap/expect, and no format!("{:?}") in the new production code.

No injection found. The engine<->survey edge is two closed, deny-unknown-fields records (Survey in, Surveyed out) parsed once into types; the engine pins the reply's bootstrap path to its own canonical current_exe; the survey is launched as Command::new(bootstrap).args(["broker","survey"]) with no shell and no interpolation, stderr nulled, in its own process group. The driver-facing carrier `capability_servers` is always removed and rewritten from the compiled McpContribution by SiteMarks::servers for every site that calls marks().site (single, panel member, sequence single step); panel/sequence member inputs are rebuilt from named fields and dialect steps build a fresh driver_input, so a recipe/result cannot smuggle the carrier. The carrier holds only server/capability/tools/discovery_tool names, no plan, store or ledger locator.

No secret or model prose reaches the journal. The only new journal write is EffectFailed {effect_id, attempt_id, error: refusal.to_string()}: every Unprovisioned variant is a fixed string, a capability name, or a transparent Refusal whose only variable field (Refusal::Name) carries a decision-0012 binding NAME, never a value. Plans and the inventory are written owner-only (dirs 0700, files 0600, O_EXCL/O_NOFOLLOW) under the protected root and read only by broker serve; the plan's `secrets` are binding names, and `environment` is fixed names, not values.

Fail-closed behavior holds and the D1/D2 changes do not weaken it. In provisioned, the budget (share) and every holding's seal are judged before the host is consulted, and the attempt directory is made exclusively with the inventory written last; any refusal appends EffectFailed and provision_with returns Ok(false), so execute returns before any driver spawns. D1's eager Host::of is stored as a Result and still consulted only after slots/seal/budget and only when a site brokers a holding, so an unreadable HOME refuses exactly the brokered attempts and never a non-brokered one (bound in provisioning_leaves_the_driver_only_what_it_did_not_spend). D1's Surveyor deadline is threaded from the same (began, *bound) through startup/left with no behavior change. D2's record_sites is a behavior-preserving extraction of the provenance/boundary writes. The tether refuses Refusal::Identity before arming the watcher unless the survey leads its own group, so a caller's group is never killed, and all exits are KILL+reap.

Residual security findings (no high/critical; not a hold):
- LOW (L1, already recorded as an open follow-up): crates/brokkr-cli/src/broker/survey.rs maps both a failed group-leader check and a failed watcher-thread spawn to Refusal::Identity. Both refuse, so this is not fail-open, but the cause is imprecise; a protocol cause of its own is outside this unit (protocol change out of scope).
- LOW/INFO (I1, already recorded): crates/brokkr-runtime/src/engine/broker.rs:328 folds self.run_id into the protected-root path walked by protected(), but the dispatch path's forge_run_id is validated only as non-empty (crates/brokkr-core/src/dispatch.rs:251); a value containing '/' or '..' reaches mkdirat/openat as one name, whose intermediate components O_NOFOLLOW does not guard, so the engine can be made to create owner-only directories and plan files outside the intended HOME/.local/state/brokkr/capabilities/<repo>/<run> root. It cannot overwrite or redirect a trusted plan (O_EXCL; broker serve's Owner/locator check refuses the mismatched layout), the created bytes carry no secret values, and the path is dormant while the MCP compile fence stands (slots empty => no host/path work), so severity stays low. Recommend the portable-path-component gate that import_run already applies to adopted ids be applied to forge_run_id/resume ids before U9b lifts the fence.

I verified the run's signed commit and clean diff; the unit's D1/D2 defects are closed as described and the controller's 559c16e5 test fix is preserved. No high or critical unresolved finding, so no security-hold.

members.security: Security review of 8819b7ee..968e6a51 (engine.rs, engine/broker.rs, engine/marks.rs, bundle.rs re-export, runtime Cargo.toml rustix process feature, cli broker/survey.rs). No finding above info. Fail-closed paths hold. (1) Budget and every holding's seal are judged before the host is consulted. A bad HOME or bootstrap refuses only an attempt that brokers a holding, and native/no-MCP attempts provision nothing. (2) The protected root is walked from / one component at a time with openat O_NOFOLLOW and fstat on the held fd, so there is no TOCTOU. HOME's ancestors must be the user's or root's and not group/other-writable unless root-owned and sticky. capabilities/<repo>/<run> must be the user's alone at 0700. The attempt directory is made exclusively, and EEXIST refuses as Provisioned, so retry, resume or reconnect cannot mint fresh budget. Plans and the inventory are written O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW at 0600 and synced, the inventory last, so a provisioning cut short leaves none and the broker refuses it as unbound. (3) The survey child is the canonical current_exe, run in its own process group with stderr discarded. Its reply is capped at 1 MiB+1 and must be one closed line, whose self-reported bootstrap path must equal the one spawned. The group is SIGKILLed before the leader is reaped, so a recycled pgid cannot be hit. Expiry refuses with Expired. (4) The survey reads exactly one request line within 1 MiB and refuses unless it leads its own group, so a caller's group is never killed. Its watcher kills the whole group on stdin EOF, which the engine holds open until it has the reply. (5) Journal: EffectFailed carries only Unprovisioned's closed Display text. Unsealed names the operator's capability, and Refusal/Unread are closed enums from our own binary. No secret value, store or ledger locator, plan path or model prose reaches the journal or the prompt. The driver-input carrier capability_servers holds only server, capability, tool names and the discovery tool, and is cleared before every write. Plans carry binding names, never values. (6) No unsafe code; the rustix process feature is the version already locked. Info-only observations, none a fail-open: (a) marks.rs brokered() maps a runtime McpIntent::contribution Err (Unservable) to no servers instead of refusing. Compile already refuses those cases and the MCP compile fence stands until U9b; the direction grants nothing. (b) survey.rs maps watcher-thread spawn failure to Refusal::Identity (run 4's L1), a mislabelled cause that still refuses; it stays a recorded follow-up. (c) Run by hand as the first stage of a shell pipeline, the hidden survey verb would lead the group and kill its pipeline peers on EOF. Operator-invoked only, with no engine path. Read-only: no files changed and nothing committed.
